questions.stem: Two senior developers disagree publicly about the architecture during a sprint review. The project manager should FIRST:
options: Escalate to the sponsor for a decision.
Meet both developers privately to understand the underlying concerns.
Choose the architecture proposed by the more experienced developer.
Add the item to the risk register and continue the review.
questions.explanation: Conflict is addressed early, directly and collaboratively. Understanding each party's concerns comes before any decision or escalation.

rationales.A: Escalating first skips the project manager's own responsibility to manage team conflict.
rationales.C: Seniority is not a basis for resolving a technical disagreement.
rationales.D: Logging a risk does not address an active conflict.

questions.source: Example Exam Content Outline v1, Execution, task 1

questions.stem: A key stakeholder has stopped attending status meetings and is not answering emails. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause the project manager should investigate first?
options: The stakeholder's engagement level has changed since the stakeholder register was last updated.
The meeting invitations are being sent to the wrong address.
The stakeholder has left the organisation.
The project has been cancelled without notice.
questions.explanation: A change in engagement is the common case and is what the stakeholder engagement plan exists to detect and manage; the other options are possible but far less likely and would be discovered on the way.

questions.stem: The final deliverable has been accepted by the customer. What should the project manager do NEXT?
options: Archive project documents and capture lessons learned.
Request additional budget for warranty support.
questions.explanation: Closing activities follow acceptance: documents are archived, lessons learned are captured and only then are resources released.
